persistence_invariants.brief: The up migration (add batch_number/serial_number, backfill, drop inventory_code) has a down migration that re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs it from location + batch + serial; up then down leaves the schema and conforming rows round-tripped (reconstruction is lossy only for nonconforming rows left NULL). VERIFIED BY A kind:fitness TEST MARKED @pytest.mark.migration ON AN ISOLATED EPHEMERAL BRANCH, never by downgrading the shared verify branch (canon: do not downgrade the shared verify database).
The UNIQUE(sku, location) key established in F1 survives this migration unchanged; splitting the code neither drops nor duplicates the constraint and location stays the canonical addressing column.

batch_number and serial_number are added as NULLABLE (no NOT NULL): nonconforming codes must persist as NULL rather than being defaulted or forcing the row out, so the columns carry no NOT NULL constraint.

Every pre-migration stock row (quantity, sku, location) is still present and retrievable after the up migration; no row is dropped whether or not its code parsed. VERIFIED BY THE ISOLATED kind:fitness @pytest.mark.migration TEST (same isolated ephemeral branch as PI1/AC6): seed a mixed pre-migration seed, run `alembic upgrade`, then assert every seeded row survives with quantity/sku/location intact. NOT verifiable on the shared UP-state branch, the migration is already applied there so pre-migration rows cannot be seeded and the up migration cannot be observed in flight.

nfrs.brief: Every sprint-1 stock row survives the schema refactor with no loss: conforming codes backfill batch/serial, nonconforming codes persist with NULL batch/serial, and no row is dropped. Backfill VALUE correctness (AC1/AC2 batch/serial populated or NULL) is asserted on the shared UP-state branch; whole-row SURVIVAL across the up migration (PI4) is asserted by the isolated @pytest.mark.migration fitness test (seed pre-migration rows -> upgrade -> assert survival), since the shared branch cannot seed pre-migration rows.
UNIQUE(sku, location) is preserved through the migration; location remains canonical and is never overwritten from the code's leading segment.

All acceptance tests run against a real Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL) with Alembic migrations applied; no mock, stub, or in-memory DB. UP-state behavior tests (AC1-AC5) run on the shared verify branch; the DOWN migration (AC6) is exercised only by a kind:fitness @pytest.mark.migration test on an ISOLATED ephemeral branch (up-then-down round-trip), because downgrading the shared branch would drop batch_number/serial_number and break every UP-state test.

The migration is reversible: the down path reconstructs inventory_code from location + batch + serial and restores the combined column, enabling rollback during rollout (additive-where-possible preference). The reverse path is exercised ONLY on an isolated ephemeral branch by a kind:fitness @pytest.mark.migration test (up-then-down round-trip); the shared verify branch is never downgraded, so AC1-AC5's UP-state behavior tests stay valid.

A migration-time integrity probe reports the count of nonconforming rows (codes that could not be parsed into batch and serial) for review before the change is accepted; delimiter-only parsing, no fabrication.
N/A for S1 (a headless schema migration with no UI surface); the boundary stays a React SPA + JSON API for the downstream S2 view story, inheriting the F1 convention. No server-rendered HTML.

The stock view is served by the React SPA (client/) over the app/routes JSON API, not server-rendered HTML. batch_number and serial_number render as two separately labelled entries (AC1) wherever the retired combined inventory_code used to appear (AC3), so the operator reads two distinct identities on the warehouse tablet with client-side navigation.

A stock row with a NULL batch or serial (nonconforming code left NULL in S1, PI3) renders cleanly: the SPA maps JSON null to an explicit 'none yet' indicator (AC2) rather than a blank region or a null crash, honoring the nfrs.md 'missing optional detail renders cleanly' preference.

The view is read-only and never fabricates or coerces values: a NULL field is surfaced as 'none yet', never as an empty string or invented value, and a populated field shows exactly the persisted batch/serial. The boundary passes model values through unchanged (no service/repository defaulting), so the displayed identity matches the S1-persisted row.

The combined inventory_code is fully retired from the read path: the boundary serializer emits no inventory_code key and the client stock-view component references no combined-code field (AC3), so no orphaned reference to the dropped column survives after the S1 refactor.

The app/routes JSON payload (both fields present, NULL emitted as JSON null, no inventory_code key) is covered by real Lakebase-branch integration tests (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL, migrations applied, no mock/stub/in-memory), per R4. The SPA render behavior (distinct labels, 'none yet', absence of combined code) is covered by the client's own component test harness, per R5.

N/A beyond the substrate default: this read-only view adds no new persistence or state transition, so it needs no dedicated audit/metric surface. Role/agent-log observability remains the substrate invariant (per nfrs.md note); the SPA and boundary emit no additional domain events for a read.
